ak_hot_dog_wall.blurb: Hot Dog Wall is a small bolted cliff in south-central Alaska, set back from the Seward Highway rather than beside it, so the visit starts with a drive and then a real walk in. Eight sport lines are recorded here, running from easy 5.7 territory through the mid grades into the low 5.13 range, with a few projects still waiting. Most routes begin from a ledge gained by an approach pitch, which makes it a place for climbers comfortable with some exposure at the base. The stone is generally solid by Turnagain Arm standards, and the wall is regarded as one of the better sport venues in the region. Going earlier in the season keeps the brushy approach manageable.
